camera_graph.cycle_closure: R_bc @ R_ab @ R_ac.T == I (a->b then b->c equals a->c)
camera_graph.note: cycle residuals are rotation-only (two-view translation is scale-free); a large residual means the pair poses disagree around the loop, not that a camera is wrong

gt_covisibility.note: the reference model's co-visibility is an upper bound from a different reconstruction; coverage measures whether the pair set could support that topology at all

reference_pose_comparison.reference: relative rotation from the reference model (gauge-free: a pair rotation does not depend on the world frame)

pose_graph.method: IRLS rotation averaging on SO(3) (right perturbations, Huber 1.0 deg, 40 iterations, one root per component pinned to identity), 2 fitting pass(es) over the accepted edges

pose_graph.bridge_note: a bridge has no cycle through it: the part it connects can be rotated about it without changing any accepted residual, so that placement is unverified

unobservable.reason: every incident edge is a bridge, so nothing constrains its rotation against the rest of the graph (a rigid rotation about the bridge is free)

observability.definition: a camera is rotation-observable when it has at least one accepted edge that lies on a cycle; an edge with no cycle (bridge) cannot verify anything

rotation_uncertainty_deg.note: RMS of a camera's incident accepted-edge residuals divided by sqrt(deg-1): the spread of the fit around it, NOT a confidence interval, and not comparable to the per-camera reference error

translation.reason: the solved layout is not physical: 1 baseline(s) are pinned at zero, which folds two cameras onto one point. Unit two-view directions with one unknown scale per edge admit layouts that fit every edge and are not camera configurations (reproduced with EXACT reference directions), so this result is not used for any centre accuracy claim

translation_observability.note: a camera with one incident direction has its position fixed only along a ray; its distance is set by the edge's unknown baseline, so its placement is not observable
